hindi: इसके आगे मत्स्यण्डिका, खण्ड और शर्करा उत्तरोत्तर अधिक निर्मल हैं; जैसे-जैसे इनकी निर्मलता होती है, वैसे-वैसे शीतलता होती है।
english: After that, matsyaṇḍikā, khaṇḍa and śarkarā (sugar) are purer still; according as their purity is, so is their coolness.
notes: tataḥ 'after that' continues from guḍa in the preceding unit (dhautaḥ svalpamalo guḍaḥ); param 'further, beyond' is taken as 'purer still'. matsyaṇḍikā, khaṇḍa and śarkarā are kept as the names of the sugar products. The Hindi 'उत्तरोत्तर' renders param.

words.gloss: wholesome for the wasted and the injured

hindi: गुडशर्करा वृष्य, क्षीण और क्षत (व्यक्तियों) के लिए हितकर तथा स्नेह से युक्त है; यासशर्करा कषाय-मधुर, शीत और तिक्तता से युक्त है।
english: Sugar from guḍa (guḍaśarkarā) is aphrodisiac, wholesome for the wasted and the injured, and has unctuousness (sneha); sugar from yāsa (yāsaśarkarā) is astringent and sweet, cold, and has bitterness.
notes: yāsa is kept as the name of the plant. kṣīṇa 'wasted' and kṣata 'injured' are taken as persons (understood).

words.gram: f. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first)

hindi: मधुशर्करा रूक्ष, वमि और अतिसार को नष्ट करने वाली तथा छेदनी है। तृष्णा, असृक्पित्त और दाह में सब शर्कराएँ प्रशस्त हैं।
english: Sugar from honey (madhuśarkarā) is dry, destroys vomiting and diarrhoea, and is cutting (chedana). All sugars are commended in thirst, asṛkpitta and burning.
notes: The 'cch' of cchedanī is the ch doubled after a long vowel (sandhi); the word is chedanī. asṛkpitta kept Sanskrit.

hindi: माक्षिक, भ्रामर, क्षौद्र और पौत्तिक — ये मधु की जातियाँ हैं। उनमें माक्षिक श्रेष्ठ है; भ्रामर विशेष रूप से गुरु है।
english: Mākṣika, bhrāmara, kṣaudra and pauttika are the kinds of honey (madhu). Of them mākṣika is the best; bhrāmara is especially heavy.

text_flags.why: possible: the same kind of honey is printed pauttikam in the next unit of this chunk (244, ghṛtavarṇaṃ tu pauttikam); paittika 'relating to Pitta' does not fit a list of honeys

notes: The four honey names are derived words and are kept as names, not split.

hindi: माक्षिक तेल के रंग का होता है, पर पौत्तिक घी के रंग का; क्षौद्र कपिल वर्ण का होता है; भ्रामर श्वेत कहा जाता है।
english: Mākṣika is of the colour of oil, but pauttika of the colour of ghee; kṣaudra is tawny (kapila) in colour; bhrāmara is said to be white.
notes: The optative syāt is rendered as a plain statement ('is').

words.gram: n. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first)
n. nom. sg., agent noun sam-√dhā

hindi: मधु वातल, गुरु और शीत, रक्तपित्त और कफ को दूर करने वाला, सन्धानकारी, छेदन, रूक्ष, कषाय और मधुर है।
english: Honey (madhu) increases Vāta, is heavy and cold, removes raktapitta and Kapha, and is uniting (sandhātṛ), cutting (chedana), dry, astringent and sweet.
notes: The 'cch' of cchedanaṃ is the ch doubled after the short vowel ṛ (sandhi); the word is chedanam.

words.gloss: because of its connection with poison
because of being heavy, dry and astringent

hindi: मधु गरम (लिया जाए) तो, अथवा उष्णता से पीड़ित (मनुष्य) को, विष से सम्बन्ध के कारण मार सकता है। गुरु, रूक्ष और कषाय होने से तथा शीतलता के कारण थोड़ा मधु हितकर है।
english: Honey may kill when (taken) hot, or (it may kill) one afflicted by heat, because of its connection with poison. Because it is heavy, dry and astringent, and because of its coldness, honey (taken) in a little (quantity) is wholesome.

text_flags.why: possible: ca + alpaṃ joins as cālpaṃ (a + a = ā); the printed 'calpaṃ' lacks the long ā. The syllable is heavy either way (before lp), so the metre does not decide

notes: uṣṇam is taken with madhu (honey that is hot) and uṣṇārtam as the person it may kill; the line can also be read 'hot honey may kill one afflicted by heat'. saviṣānvaya literally 'connection with (what is) with poison'.

words.gloss: because of being contrary to the measures of treatment

hindi: इससे — मध्वाम से — अधिक कष्टदायक कुछ नहीं है; क्योंकि उपक्रम का विरोधी होने के कारण वह मनुष्य को विष की भाँति तुरन्त मार सकता है।
english: Nothing is graver (kaṣṭatama) than this, than madhvāma (āma, undigested matter, from honey); for, because it is contrary to the measures of treatment (upakrama), it may kill a man at once, like poison.

text_flags.why: there is no stem virochin; the sense 'contrary' is the root √rudh with vi-, which the next unit of this chunk uses for the same point (248, sā madhvāme virudhyate)

notes: ataḥ and madhvāmāt are both ablatives of comparison with the superlative kaṣṭatama; English uses 'graver'. madhvāma = āma (undigested matter) arising from honey; āma kept Sanskrit.

hindi: आम में उष्णता सहित क्रिया करनी चाहिए; वह मध्वाम में विरुद्ध होती है। इसलिए मध्वाम दारुण है; वह विष की भाँति तुरन्त मार सकता है।
english: In āma, treatment with heat is to be done; that is incompatible in madhvāma. Therefore madhvāma is dreadful (dāruṇa); it may kill at once, like poison.
notes: madhvāma is printed with neuter forms here (madhvāmaṃ dāruṇaṃ), while āma is masculine in āme; the forms are kept. Line 2 repeats the second half of line 2 of 247 (sadyo hanyādyathā viṣam).

words.gloss: because of being composed of various substances

hindi: और अनेक द्रव्यों से बना होने के कारण मधु परम योगवाही है। प्रायः इक्षु-विकारों वाला यह वर्ग दसवाँ माना गया है।
english: And because it is composed of various substances, honey is a supreme yogavāhin (carrier in combination). This group, consisting mostly of sugarcane (ikṣu) products, is held to be the tenth.
notes: Both half-verses are typed on one line, with a danda after madhu inside it; the danda is left out of the split. yogavāhin literally 'carrying (the effect of) a combination'; kept Sanskrit. iti closes the group and is not translated separately. param may also be read as an adverb, 'supremely'.

words.gloss: removing hunger, thirst, languor, weakness, kukṣi diseases and fever

hindi: अब कृतान्न वर्ग: पेया क्षुधा, तृष्णा, ग्लानि, दुर्बलता, कुक्षिरोग और ज्वर को दूर करने वाली, स्वेद और अग्नि को उत्पन्न करने वाली तथा वायु और मल का अनुलोमन करने वाली है।
english: Now the group of prepared foods: thin gruel (peyā) removes hunger, thirst, languor, weakness, kukṣi diseases and fever, produces sweat and digestive fire (agni), and moves wind and faeces downward.
notes: The heading 'atha kṛtānnavargaḥ' is typed on the verse line, outside the metre; the dashes are left out. vāta beside varcas (faeces) is taken as wind released from the body (Hindi वायु); 'Vāta' is the alternative. varco'nulomanī is printed without the avagraha. kukṣi kept Sanskrit.

hindi: विलेपिका भी तर्पणी, ग्राहिणी, लघु और हृद्य है। पर मण्ड अग्नि को दीप्त करता है और वात का अनुलोमन भी करता है,
english: Vilepikā also is replenishing (tarpaṇa), binding, light and pleasing to the heart. But maṇḍa kindles the digestive fire (agni) and also moves Vāta downward,

text_flags.why: there is no stem ladhu; the feminine of laghu 'light' is laghvī, and this chunk has laghu forms (laghavo 257, laghavaḥ 264)

notes: SENTENCE: the description of maṇḍa continues in 252 and 253. vilepikā and maṇḍa kept Sanskrit. The optative anulomayet is rendered as a statement.

hindi: स्रोतों को मृदु करता है और स्वेद भी उत्पन्न करता है। लङ्घन किए हुओं, विरेचन किए हुओं, और स्नेह के पच जाने पर प्यासे लोगों के लिए —
english: softens the channels (srotas) and also produces sweat. For the lightened, the purged, and those who are thirsty when the sneha (unctuous substance) has been digested,
notes: SENTENCE: line 1 continues maṇḍa from 251; line 2 begins a sentence completed in 253 (maṇḍaḥ syāt prāṇadhāraṇaḥ). jīrṇe snehe is a locative absolute. The genitives are rendered 'for'.

hindi: मण्ड दीपन और लघु होने के कारण प्राणों को धारण करने वाला होता है। पर लाजपेया, जिसका कण्ठ सूखा हो उस देहधारी के लिए, श्रम को नष्ट करने वाली है।
english: maṇḍa, because it stimulates digestion and is light, would sustain life. But lājapeyā (thin gruel of parched grain) destroys fatigue for a person whose throat is dried up (kṣāma).
notes: SENTENCE: line 1 completes 252. kṣāma 'dried up, thin'; 'weak' is the alternative. The genitive dehinaḥ is rendered 'for'. The masculine forms of 254 line 1 do not agree with lājapeyā; they go with lājamaṇḍaḥ in 254.

words.gloss: bringing about balance of the dhātus

hindi: लाजमण्ड तृष्णा और अतीसार को शान्त करने वाला, धातुसाम्य करने वाला, शिव, अग्नि को उत्पन्न करने वाला तथा दाह और मूर्च्छा को दूर करने वाला है।
english: Lājamaṇḍa (maṇḍa of parched grain) allays thirst and diarrhoea, brings about the balance of the dhātus, is wholesome (śiva), produces digestive fire (agni) and wards off burning and mūrcchā.
notes: Line 1 (masculine) is taken with lājamaṇḍaḥ of line 2. atīsāra is printed with long ī (= atisāra). mūrcchā kept Sanskrit.

words.gloss: for those of weak fire and of irregular fire
words.gram: m. gen. pl., dvandva of bahuvrīhis

words.gloss: for children, the old and women

hindi: मन्दाग्नि और विषमाग्नि वालों को, बालकों, वृद्धों और स्त्रियों को, तथा सुकुमारों को भली-भाँति संस्कृत लाजमण्ड देना चाहिए।
english: And well-prepared lājamaṇḍa is to be given to those whose digestive fire (agni) is weak and those whose digestive fire is irregular, to children, the old and women, and to the delicate.
notes: The genitives are rendered 'to' (recipients).

hindi: पिप्पली और शुण्ठी के साथ पकाया गया तथा लाजा और खट्टे दाडिम से युक्त (लाजमण्ड) क्षुधा और पिपासा को दूर करने वाला, पथ्य, और शुद्ध हुए लोगों के मल को दूर करने वाला है।
english: Boiled with pippalī and śuṇṭhī and combined with lāja and sour dāḍima, (lājamaṇḍa) removes hunger and thirst, is wholesome (pathya), and removes waste (mala) for those who have been purified.
notes: The subject is understood from 255 (lājamaṇḍa); the masculine forms agree. śuddhānām 'of the purified' is taken as those who have undergone purification. lājāmladāḍimaiḥ may also be read as three items: lāja, sour things and dāḍima. pippali- is printed with short i in the compound and kept. Common names: pippalī = long pepper, śuṇṭhī = dry ginger, dāḍima = pomegranate.

hindi: लाजसक्तु कषाय-मधुर, शीत और लघु होते हैं। भली-भाँति धोया हुआ, निथारा हुआ, पका हुआ और गरम ओदन लघु होता है।
english: Saktus of lāja (parched grain) are astringent and sweet, cold and light. Boiled rice (odana) that is well washed, drained, cooked and warm is light.
notes: prasruta 'drained' (literally 'flowed off'), taken as the cooking water poured off. svinna here 'cooked (by boiling)'. saktu kept Sanskrit.

words.gloss: in gara and in diseases of śleṣman

hindi: गर और श्लेष्मा के रोगों में भी भुने चावलों से बना (ओदन) चाहते हैं। बिना धोया, बिना निथारा, बिना पका और ठंडा भी ओदन गुरु होता है।
english: They want (odana) made of roasted rice grains also in gara and in diseases of śleṣman (Kapha). Odana that is unwashed, undrained, not cooked, and also cold, is heavy.
notes: The noun odana of line 1 is understood from 257; icchanti has no stated subject ('they', understood). gara kept Sanskrit.

words.gloss: odanas with meat, vegetables, muscle-fat, oil, ghee, marrow and fruit

hindi: मांस, शाक, वसा, तैल, घृत, मज्जा और फल के ओदन बलकारक, सन्तर्पण, हृद्य और गुरु होते हैं तथा बृंहण करते हैं।
english: Odanas (boiled rice) with meat, vegetables (śāka), muscle-fat (vasā), oil, ghee, marrow and fruit are strengthening, replenishing (saṃtarpaṇa), pleasing to the heart and heavy, and they nourish (bṛṃhaṇa).
notes: majja- is the compound form of majjan 'marrow'.

words.gloss: prepared in combination with māṣa, tila, milk and mudga
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first), ppp. caus. √sādh

hindi: उसी प्रकार माष, तिल, दूध और मुद्ग के संयोग से सिद्ध किए गए (ओदन) होते हैं। कुल्माष गुरु, रूक्ष, वातल और मल को भेदने वाले होते हैं।
english: Likewise are (odanas) prepared in combination with māṣa, tila, milk and mudga. Kulmāṣas are heavy, dry, increase Vāta and loosen the faeces.
notes: Line 1 is taken with the odanas of 259 (tadvat 'like them'); it may instead describe the kulmāṣas of line 2. bhinnavarcas literally 'having broken (loose) faeces'. kulmāṣa kept Sanskrit. Common names: māṣa = black gram, tila = sesame.

words.gloss: made of pulses, of godhūma and of yava

hindi: सूप्य, गोधूम और यव से बने जो कोई उबले हुए भक्ष्य हैं, वैद्य उनकी गुरुता और लघुता द्रव्य के अनुसार बताए।
english: Whatever boiled eatables there are, made of pulses (sūpya), of godhūma and of yava, the physician should declare their heaviness and lightness according to the substance.
notes: saupya, gaudhūma and yāvika are derived words ('made of pulse, wheat, barley') and are not split further. Common names: godhūma = wheat, yava = barley.

words.gram: m. acc. sg. ppp. √kṛ with a-

words.gloss: in succession, each later one more

hindi: अकृत और कृत यूष, पतला और संस्कारित रस, तथा अम्ल और अनम्ल सूप — इन्हें उत्तरोत्तर गुरु जानना चाहिए।
english: Unprepared and prepared yūṣa, thin and processed rasa (meat-juice), and sour and non-sour sūpa: one should know (them) as heavy in succession (yathottaram).
notes: akṛtaṃ kṛtayūṣaṃ is taken as akṛta (yūṣa) and kṛta yūṣa, 'unprepared' and 'prepared' (without and with seasoning). rasa in this food list = meat-juice. yathottaram may apply within each pair or along the whole list; the text does not decide. sāṃskārika is a derived word, not split.

hindi: सक्तु वातल, रूक्ष और बहुत मल का अनुलोमन करने वाले हैं; पिए जाने पर वे मनुष्य का तुरन्त तर्पण करते हैं और वे तुरन्त बल देने वाले हैं।
english: Saktus increase Vāta, are dry and move much faeces downward; drunk, they replenish a man at once, and they give strength at once.
notes: varco'nulominaḥ is printed without the avagraha. sadyobala literally 'whose strength is immediate'.

hindi: शालि से बने सक्तु मधुर, लघु, शीत, ग्राही, रक्तपित्त-नाशक तथा तृष्णा, छर्दि और ज्वर को दूर करने वाले हैं।
english: Saktus made from śāli (rice) are sweet, light and cold, binding, destroy raktapitta, and remove thirst, vomiting and fever.

words.gloss: udāvarta, coryza, cough, meha and galagraha

hindi: यवापूप, यावक और वाड्य भी उदावर्त, प्रतिश्याय, कास, मेह और गलग्रह — इन व्याधियों को नष्ट कर सकते हैं।
english: Yavāpūpa (cake of yava), yāvaka and vāḍya too would destroy the diseases udāvarta, pratiśyāya (coryza), cough (kāsa), meha and galagraha.
notes: vāḍya is not otherwise known in this form; it is kept as printed, and its meaning (a preparation, by the context of yava foods) is uncertain. The singular verb hanyāt goes with each of the three subjects. udāvarta, meha, galagraha kept Sanskrit.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., gerundive (kṛtya) √bhakṣ as noun

hindi: धाना नाम वाले जो भक्ष्य हैं, वे प्रायः लेखन स्वभाव वाले हैं; शुष्क होने के कारण तर्पण हैं, और विष्टम्भी होने के कारण दुर्जर हैं।
english: The eatables called dhānā are mostly reducing (lekhana) in nature; because of dryness (they are) replenishing (tarpaṇa), and because of being obstructive, hard to digest.
notes: The link of 'because of dryness' with 'replenishing' is hard in sense; śuṣkatvāt may instead give the reason for lekhanātmakāḥ of line 1. A form atarpaṇāḥ 'non-replenishing' would add a syllable to the 8-syllable quarter (śuṣkatvāttarpaṇāścaiva has 8), so the printed tarpaṇāḥ is kept; no flag. dhānā kept Sanskrit (roasted grain). eva is not rendered separately.

hindi: विरूढ धाना, शष्कुली, पिण्डकों सहित मधुक्रोड, पूप, पूपलिका आदि पैष्टिक (भक्ष्य) अत्यन्त गुरु होते हैं।
english: Sprouted dhānā, śaṣkulīs, madhukroḍas along with piṇḍakas, pūpas (cakes), pūpalikās and the rest, made of flour (paiṣṭika), are extremely heavy.

text_flags.why: the m. nom. pl. of guru is guravaḥ, as printed in this chunk (guravaḥ 270, guravo 259, 260); 'guruvaḥ' is not a form

notes: virūḍhadhānā is printed without visarga before śaṣkulyo; it is taken as plural (dhānāḥ) with the other plurals; a feminine singular is also possible. The preparation names are kept Sanskrit. paiṣṭika 'made of flour (piṣṭa)' is a derived word, not split.

words.gloss: prepared with fruit, meat, muscle-fat, vegetables, palala and honey
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first), ppp. sam-√kṛ

hindi: फल, मांस, वसा, शाक, पलल और क्षौद्र से संस्कृत भक्ष्य वृष्य और बलकारक, गुरु तथा बृंहण स्वभाव वाले होते हैं।
english: Eatables prepared with fruit, meat, muscle-fat (vasā), vegetables (śāka), palala and honey (kṣaudra) are aphrodisiac and strengthening, heavy and nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa) in nature.
notes: palala kept Sanskrit (sesame paste).

words.gloss: pūpakas of milk and sugarcane juice

hindi: वेशवार गुरु, स्निग्ध तथा बल और उपचय को बढ़ाने वाला है। दूध और इक्षुरस के पूपक गुरु, तर्पण और वृष्य होते हैं।
english: Veśavāra is heavy and unctuous, and increases strength and increase of body (upacaya). Pūpakas (cakes) of milk and sugarcane juice are heavy, replenishing (tarpaṇa) and aphrodisiac.
notes: veśavāra kept Sanskrit as the name of a preparation; the text does not describe it here.

hindi: गुड सहित, तिल सहित तथा दूध, क्षौद्र और शर्करा सहित भक्ष्य वृष्य और बलकारक हैं, पर अत्यन्त गुरु माने गए हैं।
english: Eatables with guḍa, with tila, and with milk, honey (kṣaudra) and sugar (śarkarā) are aphrodisiac and strengthening, but are held to be extremely heavy.
notes: eva in satilāścaiva is not rendered separately.

hindi: स्नेह सहित और स्नेह में सिद्ध, विविध लक्षणों वाले गोधूम के भक्ष्य गुरु, तर्पण, वृष्य और हृद्य माने गए हैं।
english: Eatables of various characteristics made of godhūma, with sneha and prepared in sneha, are considered heavy, replenishing (tarpaṇa), aphrodisiac and pleasing to the heart.
notes: gaudhūmika is a derived word ('made of godhūma'), not split.

words.gloss: dhānā, parpaṭa, pūpa and the rest

hindi: गोधूम के और पैष्टिक भक्ष्य, तथा धाना, पर्पट, पूप आदि संस्कार से लघु होते हैं; उन्हें जानकर वैसा निर्देश करे।
english: There are eatables of godhūma and of flour (paiṣṭika), dhānā, parpaṭa, pūpa and the rest, that are light through processing (saṃskāra); having understood them, one should declare (them) accordingly.
notes: gaudhūmapaiṣṭika may also be read 'flour preparations of godhūma' (one class). parpaṭa kept Sanskrit.

hindi: पृथुक गुरु होते हैं; उन्हें भूनकर, पर थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में, खाना चाहिए। यावा विष्टम्भ करके पचते हैं; रस सहित वे मल को भेदने वाले होते हैं।
english: Pṛthukas are heavy; one should eat them roasted, but in small quantities. Yāvas (preparations of yava) are digested after causing obstruction; with juice (sarasa) they loosen the faeces.
notes: pṛthuka kept Sanskrit (flattened grain). yāva 'made of yava' is a derived word. sarasa may also mean 'with flavour (rasa)'; 'with juice' is given. jīryanti is class-4 with passive sense.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa, ppp. vi-√kṛ

words.gloss: with pungent things, sneha and salt

hindi: सूप्य अन्न से बने भक्ष्य वातल, रूक्ष और शीतल होते हैं; उन्हें कटु, स्नेह और लवण सहित, थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में खाना चाहिए।
english: Eatables made from pulse grains (sūpya) increase Vāta and are dry and cold; one should eat them with pungent things, sneha and salt, and in small quantities.

words.gram: m. nom. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first)

hindi: जो भक्ष्य मृदुपाक हैं और जो स्थूल और कठिन हैं, वे गुरु, देर से पचने वाले, तथा पुष्टि और बल देने वाले होते हैं।
english: Eatables that are soft-cooked (mṛdupāka), and those that are thick and hard, are heavy, of delayed digestion (vyatikrāntapāka), and give nourishment and strength.
notes: vyatikrāntapāka literally 'whose pāka has gone beyond'; taken as digestion that exceeds its time; 'whose cooking is overdone' is the alternative. mṛdupāka 'soft-cooked' may also mean 'mildly cooked'.

hindi: द्रव्य, संयोग और संस्कार को, तथा उसी प्रकार द्रव्य के मान को अलग-अलग जानकर, भक्ष्यों की गुरुता और लघुता अपनी-अपनी (प्रकृति) के अनुसार बताए।
english: Having understood the substance, combination and processing, and likewise the quantity of the substance, separately, one should declare the heaviness and lightness of eatables, each according to its own (nature).

hindi: पके, कच्चे, भिगोए और भुने हुए नाना द्रव्यों से युक्त विमर्दक गुरु, हृद्य, वृष्य और बलवानों के लिए हितकर है।
english: Vimardaka, combined with various substances, cooked, raw, moistened and fried, is heavy, pleasing to the heart, aphrodisiac, and wholesome for the strong.
notes: The edition prints this verse in round brackets, with its closing danda inside ('||)'); the input does not say why. The brackets and danda are left out of the split. vimardaka kept Sanskrit as the name of a preparation. klinna 'moistened' (ppp. √klid).

hindi: रसाला बृंहणी, वृष्य, स्निग्ध, बलकारक और रुचि देने वाली है। गुड सहित दही स्नेहन, तर्पण, हृद्य और वातघ्न है।
english: Rasālā is nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa), aphrodisiac, unctuous, strengthening and gives relish (ruci). Curd (dadhi) with guḍa is oleating (snehana), replenishing (tarpaṇa), pleasing to the heart and Vāta-destroying.
notes: rasālā kept Sanskrit as the name of a preparation.

hindi: द्राक्षा, खर्जूर और कोल का, परूषक का, क्षौद्र का, और जो इक्षु-विकार को लेकर (बनता) है, वह पानक गुरु और विष्टम्भी होता है।
english: The drink (pānaka) of drākṣā, kharjūra and kola, of parūṣaka, of honey (kṣaudra), and that which is (made) with regard to sugarcane products, is heavy and obstructive.
notes: SENTENCE: the pānakas continue into the next unit (280, teṣāṃ ... pānakānām). prati 'with regard to'; 'made from' is understood. Common names: drākṣā = grape, kharjūra = date, kola = jujube; parūṣaka kept Sanskrit, not identified.
